messages:
sara (AE): 🚨 Heads-up — Acme Health POC just hit a 429 spike during the demo. They report ~15 requests in 30s and several consumer calls failing. Demo halted. Can eng help triage?

sara (AE): snippet from customer (they pasted response):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 3
X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "route quota exceeded" }
```

devon (SE): thanks, sending to eng. Are these single-shot long responses (big token counts) or many small requests?

sara (AE): mostly short chat turns (avg ~350 tokens) but they do a 10-message burst to warm up the UI.

jordan (eng-runtime): likely hitting per-route burst cap. For hosted POCs we default a conservative burst window for new accounts to avoid noisy neighbors.

jordan (eng-runtime): can you paste the route name or customer project id? I can check the quota table. Also, ask them to share the request pattern (parallel clients).

sara (AE): project_id: acme-health-poc-21. Parallel clients: 8 browsers simultaneously.

ashley (eng-sre): grabbing logs now. If it's a per-route cap we should see corresponding 429 counters in the routing service. Give me ~2 min.

sre-bot: log-query result: 2026-02-12T16:03:10Z route=chat.v1 project=acme-health-poc-21 status=429 reason=burst_limit_exceeded count=12

jordan (eng-runtime): confirmed: burst_limit_exceeded spikes on that route. Options: temporarily increase burst quota for this project, suggest reducing parallel clients to 3, or use the small-token model variant. Which do you want?

simon (sales-engineer): customer is in the demo — we need quick win. Can we bump burst to 200 req/min for 2 hours? I'll own rollback.

ashley (eng-sre): I can apply a temporary override on the quota for acme-health-poc-21. Applying now.

sre-bot: quota-change: project=acme-health-poc-21 scope=route:chat.v1 override_burst=200 ttl=2h by=ashley (eng-sre) — OK

devon (SE): while that's rolling, please advise them to add exponential backoff on 429s. Example client snippet:
```js
// simple backoff
async function requestWithBackoff(req){
  for(let i=0;i<5;i++){
    const res = await fetch(req);
    if(res.status!==429) return res;
    await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, Math.pow(2,i)*250));
  }
  throw new Error('rate limited');
}
```

sara (AE): they confirmed UI resumed after the bump, demo continued.

jordan (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) we should triage request size — 350 tokens * 8 parallel = token budget pressure. Recommend using a model variant with lower token cost or reduce batch size. 2) For long term POC, propose enabling short-lived dedicated capacity or raise baseline quota.

simon (sales-engineer): i'll send customer a summary and next steps: reduce parallelism, enable backoff, consider dedicated for steady production.

ashley (eng-sre): opened internal ticket INF-4521 to review default burst settings for new POCs and add a checklist for Sales enablement.

sara (AE): thanks everyone. Action items: ashley — confirm when override expires; devon — send the client backoff snippet and monitoring tips; simon — share guidance doc with customer. :thumbsup:

ashley (eng-sre): override TTL is 2h, i'll post another update at expiry.

jordan (eng-runtime): also flagged a per-route dashboard alert for acme-health-poc-21 so we get pro-active warnings next time.

sara (AE): perfect — closing this thread for now, will reopen if anything else pops up.
